document_check.note: Document is Gazbare P, Palekar TJ, 'Identifying mild cognitive impairment and its predictors among normal middle adulthood in Pune, Maharashtra: A community-based cross-sectional survey', Clinical Epidemiology and Global Health 2024;25:101490, doi:10.1016/j.cegh.2023.101490. It is the Indian study by Gazbare & Palekar 2024 cited for the education effect. The design is cross-sectional, not a cohort (see notes).

cited_result: Association of lower educational level with MCI (defined as ACE-III score below 88) among community adults aged 40 to 60 in Pune. The principal result is the multivariable OR versus school-level education: 0.27 (95% CI 0.15 to 0.51) for postgraduate and 0.43 (0.27 to 0.71) for graduate education.
tool_reason: The cited result is an association between education and MCI status measured at a single time point in a community survey, so the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist applies.

domains.rationale: The paper states the age range and the exclusions (prior cognitive or neurological diagnoses, illiteracy, refusal).

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Six hundred and five participants aged 40–60yrs were included. Pre-diagnosed cases of cognitive decline like dementia, alzheimer, traumatic brain injury and stroke, illiterate individuals and one who declined to participate were excluded.

domains.domain: 2. Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The paper describes the district, the multistage random ward sampling, the dates and the sociodemographic distribution (Table 1). It does not say how individuals were selected within wards, and 15 wards of 40 respondents (600) does not match the 605 reported.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: Multistage sampling technique was used in the study, conducted in Pune district that has 73 wards, out of which 15 wards were randomly selected using random number tables. 40 respondents were randomly selected from each of these wards as per the selection criteria. The data was collected from November 2019 to September 2020.

domains.rationale: Education was self-reported at interview in three categories. Self-reported education is conventionally accepted as valid, although the categories are coarse and illiterate people were excluded, which truncates the exposure range.

signalling.question: Was the exposure (level of education) measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: After written informed consent, each participant was interviewed for socio-demographic data [...] Level of Education School [...] Graduate [...] Postgraduate

domains.domain: 4. Objective, standard criteria for the condition
domains.rationale: MCI was defined only as a score below 88 on a screening test. There was no clinical assessment of cognitive complaint, functional status or exclusion of dementia, although the paper's own definition of MCI requires these. The source population for the quoted sensitivity and specificity is not stated.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition (MCI)?
signalling.quote: The cutoffs recommended for MCI is below 88 (sensitivity = 1; specificity = 0.96) for clinical purpose and 82 (sensitivity = 0.93; specificity = 1) for research. We have considered ACE-III score of less than 88 as MCI. [...] reflects the clinical situation where a person has memory complaints with objective evidence but their functional status is maintained and no sign of dementia.

domains.rationale: The paper lists sociodemographic and lifestyle confounders. It did not assess comorbidities, and the authors acknowledge this.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: 2.6.1. Potential modifier or confounders • Socio-demographic data: age, gender, marital status, type of family, level of education. • Perceived Stress Scale-10 (PSS-10)

domains.rationale: Multivariable logistic regression included all covariates simultaneously (Table 3).

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: Multivariate logistic regression models ascertained the risk factors associated with MCI.

domains.rationale: The outcome is an unadjusted ACE-III total score with a fixed cut-off. Pen-and-paper cognitive screening scores depend on education, and the paper applied no education-adjusted cut-off. Screen-positive status is therefore partly determined by the exposure itself, which biases the education association away from the null; the paper itself cites this problem (Konda et al.). The paper does not say which language version was used for whom, who administered the test, how testers were trained, or whether they were blinded. The authors concede possible assessment bias.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes (MCI status) measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Cognitive function was assessed by Addenbrooke's cognitive examination-III available in Indian English & Hindi language. [...] Konda et al. argued that illiteracy/less education shows low cognitive reserve, poor control of cerebrovascular disease risk factors, difficulties in cognitive evaluation, poor adaptation of neuropsychological test which may affect the performance on cognitive assessment. [...] The study can fall into assessment bias, selection bias.

domains.rationale: The multistage cluster sample (15 wards) was analysed with ordinary chi-square tests and logistic regression, with no allowance for clustering or design effect, so standard errors are understated. Several statistics are internally inconsistent. Stress chi-square = 2.73 is reported with p = 0.04, which is impossible for 2 df. Family-type ORs have confidence intervals spanning three orders of magnitude, suggesting sparse cells. Table 2 repeats the MCI percentages in the No MCI column for lifestyle.

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: For the analysis of categorical variables, chi-square test was used. Multivariate logistic regression models ascertained the risk factors associated with MCI. [...] stress (χ2 = 2.73, p = 0.04) [...] Extended family 1 1.60 (0.05–48.18) 0.78

overall: High risk of bias (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 4, 7 and 8 No)
overall_rationale: By the review's rule, a No on valid outcome measurement or appropriate analysis makes the overall rating high. Both apply here. MCI was a screen-positive result on an education-sensitive test with no education adjustment, which bears directly on the cited education association. The analysis also ignored the cluster sampling and contains inconsistent statistics. Sampling, eligibility and confounder adjustment were adequate.

applicability.rationale: Community adults aged 40 to 60, with illiterate people excluded. They are younger than typical MCI samples, and the lowest-education stratum is missing.
The outcome is screen-positive cognitive impairment on ACE-III, not clinically diagnosed MCI. This limits how far it can corroborate education effects found in clinically defined MCI cohorts.
